title: Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal - Week of 2025-09-01
summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Prepare For Implementation Of stUSDS - Defines the parameters of stUSDS and the process of updating them in preparation for the launch of stUSDS. Define Resolution Process For Core Simplification Buffer Budget - Defines a resolution process for the Core Simplification Buffer Budget. Update Smart Contract Risk Calculations - Revises the calculation of Smart Contract Risk to reflect the latest process and updates the list of auditors. Refine Risk Capital Requirements For Ethena - Updates the Instance Financial RRC Ratio for Ethena to account for lending Ethena related assets against other Ethena related assets. Update Responsible Party For Updating Emergency Response Group Members - Makes the Governance Facilitators responsible for updating the members of the Emergency Response Group. Add Definitions For Liquidity Layer Parameters - Adds definitions of commonly used parameters in Prime Agent Liquidity Layers. Update Accessibility Reward Logic - Clarifies the rules for how Prime Agents and Integrators can split the Accessibility Reward. Make Minor Corrections - Makes minor spelling and grammatical corrections. Prepare For Implementation Of stUSDS Add a new subdocument of A.1.9.2.2.10 - Bounded External Access Modules (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Bounded External Access Modules (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.1.9.2.2.10.2 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Bounded External Access Modules - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Exception (Core) - The stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (stUSDS BEAM) manages the parameters of the stUSDS system. Whitelisted operators can use the stUSDS BEAM to modify rates without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The stUSDS BEAM modifies stUSDS parameters within specified ranges. See A.4.4 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module. This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to update stUSDS parameters more quickly than waiting for the Governance and Spell Process execution and the GSM Pause Delay. The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting stUSDS parameters to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the stUSDS BEAM parameters and the STUSDS_MOM. Add a new subdocument of A.1.9.2.2 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly before A.1.9.2.2.12 - Linear Interpolation Module (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module (GitHub) and after A.1.9.2.2.11 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Core) - The STUSDS_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the stUSDS Bounded External Access Module or set the cap or line stUSDS parameters to zero. This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the stUSDS BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the STUSDS_MOM is activated to disable the stUSDS BEAM, the stUSDS BEAM will not be able to change any stUSDS parameters in the system. If the STUSDS_MOM has been triggered, it will still be possible to modify stUSDS parameters through the usual Executive Vote process, subject to the GSM Pause Delay. Replace A.4.4.1.2.2 - stUSDS Rate (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Rate (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - stUSDS Rate (Core) - The variable yield earned by stUSDS holders is calculated using the formula: stUSDS Rate = Sky Savings Rate + (SKY Borrow Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate) * Utilization - Rfactor * f(Utilization) A.4.4 - Parameters Definition (Core) - The parameters of the stUSDS Rate formula are further defined in the documents herein. A.4.4 Sky Savings Rate Definition (Core) - Sky Savings Rate is the Sky Savings Rate defined in A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Sky Savings Rate . A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Rate is the SKY Borrow Rate defined in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Rate . SKY Borrow Minimum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate defined in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate . A.4.4 - Utilization Definition (Core) - Utilization is the percent of funds in the stUSDS contract that are used to fund borrowing against staked SKY. A.4.4 - Utilization Calculation (Core) - The Utilization is calculated as a time-weighted utilization over a one (1) day interval. A.4.4 - Time-Weighted Utilization (Core) - The documents herein define the process to calculate time-weighted utilization. A.4.4 - Determine Start And End Times (Core) - First, the start time T_{0} and end time T_{n} of the interval, over which time-weighted utilization are to be calculated, are selected. A.4.4 - Collect Borrow And Supply Events (Core) - Data is then collected on all supply and borrow events, sorted by time, where: t_{i} is the timestamp of event i ; B_{i} is the total amount borrowed at time t_{i} ; S_{i} is the total amount supplied at time t_{i} ; and U_{i} is the utilization at time t_{i} , \frac{B_{i}}{S_{i}} . A.4.4 - Insert Synthetic Events (Core) - If t_{0} is greater than T_{0} then a synthetic event is inserted at T_{0} with values B_{0} and S_{0} . Similarly, if t_{n} is less than T_{n} then a synthetic event is inserted at T_{n} with values B_{n} and S_{n} . A.4.4 - Calculate Time-Weighted Utilization (Core) - Finally, the time-weighted utilization is calculated using the following formula: \text{Util}_{\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} U_i \cdot (t_{i+1} - t_i)}{T_n - T_0} A.4.4 - Reference Implementation (Core) - A reference implementation of the time-weighted utilization formula is included herein. The reference implementation uses sample data and a 30 day interval for illustrative purposes. # Your list of real events: (timestamp, total_borrowed, total_supply) events = [ (datetime(2025, 7, 25, 10), 100_000, 200_000), (datetime(2025, 7, 25, 16), 120_000, 210_000), (datetime(2025, 7, 26, 8), 130_000, 220_000), (datetime(2025, 7, 27, 12), 110_000, 215_000), (datetime(2025, 7, 28, 9), 140_000, 225_000), ] # Ensure events are sorted events.sort() # Get time window now = datetime.utcnow() start_time = now - timedelta(days=30) # Add synthetic first event (30d ago) using earliest known borrow/supply first_real_ts, first_borrow, first_supply = events[0] if first_real_ts start_time: events.insert(0, (start_time, first_borrow, first_supply)) # Add synthetic final event (now) using most recent known borrow/supply last_real_ts, last_borrow, last_supply = events[-1] if last_real_ts now: events.append((now, last_borrow, last_supply)) # Step 1: Compute utilization per event utilizations = [] for ts, borrow, supply in events: utilization = borrow / supply if supply != 0 else 0 utilizations.append((ts, utilization)) # Step 2: Compute time-weighted utilization average weighted_sum = 0 total_time = 0 for i in range(len(utilizations) - 1): ts1, util1 = utilizations[i] ts2, _ = utilizations[i + 1] time_diff = (ts2 - ts1).total_seconds() weighted_sum += util1 * time_diff total_time += time_diff avg_utilization = weighted_sum / total_time if total_time 0 else 0 print(f"30-day time-weighted average utilization: {avg_utilization:.2%}") A.4.4 - Rfactor Definition (Core) - Rfactor is calculated using the formula: Rfactor = \frac{2u_m - 1}{2u_m \left( u_{opt}(\alpha + 1) - 1 + \frac{\beta u_{opt}}{slope1} \right)} The parameters of this formula are specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Maximum Profit Utilization Definition (Core) - u_{m} is the maximum profit utilization. A.4.4 - Maximum Profit Utilization Current Value (Core) - The current value of u_{m} is 70%. A.4.4 - Target Utilization Definition (Core) - u_{opt} is the target utilization specified in A.4.4 Rate Setting Mechanism. A.4.4 - Alpha Definition (Core) - \alpha is calculated using the formula: alpha = ((SKY Borrow Maximum Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate) / Slope 1) - 1 The parameters of this formula are specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate is the maximum value of the SKY Borrow Rate at 100% Utilization. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate Current Value (Core) - The current value of the SKY Borrow Maximum Rate is 30%. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate specified in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate . A.4.4 - Slope 1 Definition (Core) - Slope 1 is the Slope 1 parameter specified in A.4.4 - Slope 1. A.4.4 - Beta Definition (Core) - \beta is a tuning parameter that determines how much profit is made at maximum utilization. A.4.4 - Beta Current Value (Core) - The current value of \beta is 100%. A.4.4 - Slope 1 Definition (Core) - slope1 is the Slope 1 parameter specified in A.4.4 - Slope 1. A.4.4 - Utilization Function Definition (Core) - f(Utilization) is calculated using the formula: f(Utilization) = Utilization * ((SKY Borrow Maximum Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate + Beta) * Utilization + SKY Borrow Minimum Rate - SKY Borrow Rate) The parameters of this formula are specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Utilization Definition (Core) - Utilization is the utilization as specified in A.4.4 - Utilization Definition. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate is the SKY Borrow Maximum Rate specified in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate Definition. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate specified in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate Definition. A.4.4 - Beta Definition (Core) - Beta is the beta specified in A.4.4 - Beta Definition. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Rate is the SKY Borrow Rate specified in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Rate. A.4.4 - Parameters Modification (Core) - The parameters specified in A.4.4 - Parameters Definition that are set by governance may be modified by the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors. This process will be conducted through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle or, if necessary, through out-of-schedule Executive Votes. Replace A.4.4.1.2.5.1 - Rate Setting Mechanism (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - SKY Borrow Rate - Rate Setting Mechanism (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 Rate Setting Mechanism (Core) - The SKY Borrow Rate adjusts to target a 90% utilization rate of the USDS in the stUSDS contract. When stUSDS utilization is below 90%, the rate gradually decreases; when above 90%, it gradually increases. The SKY Borrow Rate cannot fall below the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate. See A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate. The specific parameters and formula governing the rate of adjustment are specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Rate Setting Parameters (Core) - The parameters of the rate setting mechanism are specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Utilization (Core) - Utilization is the percentage of funds in the stUSDS contract that are used to fund borrowing against staked SKY specified in A.4.4 - Utilization Definition. A.4.4 - Target Utilization (Core) - Target Utilization is the target utilization rate of USDS in the stUSDS contract specified in A.4.4 Rate Setting Mechanism. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate (Core) - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is the rate that the SKY Borrow Rate cannot fall below specified in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate. A.4.4 - Slope 1 - Slope 1 represents the spread of the SKY Borrow Rate over the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate when Utilization is at Target Utilization. A.4.4 - Slope 1 Current Value (Core) - The current value of the Slope 1 parameter is 12.575%. A.4.4 - Slope 1 Modification (Core) - The Slope 1 parameter may be modified by the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors. This process will be conducted through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle or, if necessary, through out-of-schedule Executive Votes. A.4.4 - Slope 2 - Slope 2 represents the spread of the SKY Borrow Rate at 100% Utilization over the SKY Borrow Rate at Target Utilization. A.4.4 - Slope 2 Current Value (Core) - The current value of the Slope 2 parameter is 12.575%. A.4.4 - Slope 2 Modification (Core) - The Slope 2 parameter may be modified by the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors. This process will be conducted through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle or, if necessary, through out-of-schedule Executive Votes. A.4.4 - Slope 2 Methodology (Core) - Under normal circumstances governance should set the Slope 2 parameter based on the following formula: Slope 2 = Slope 1 * alpha The parameters of this formula are specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Slope 1 Definition (Core) - The Slope 1 parameter is specified in A.4.4 - Slope 1. A.4.4 - Alpha Definition (Core) - The alpha parameter is specified in A.4.4 - Alpha Definition. A.4.4 - Rate Setting Formula (Core) - The Sky Borrow Rate is calculated according to the following formula when Utilization is less than or equal to Target Utilization: SKY Borrow Rate = SKY Borrow Minimum Rate + Utilization / Target Utilization * Slope 1 The SKY Borrow Rate is calculated according to the following formula when Utilization is greater than Target Utilization: SKY Borrow Rate = SKY Borrow Minimum Rate + Slope 1 + (Utilization - Target Utilization) / (1 - Target Utilization) * Slope 2 Replace A.4.4.1.2.6 - stUSDS Risk Parameters (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Risk Parameters (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - stUSDS Risk Parameters (Core) - The liquidation parameters for SKY-backed loans funded via stUSDS are: Liquidation Ratio: 125% Calc : StairstepExponentialDecrease Tau : 0 days Tolerance : 0.5 Cut : 0.99 Step : 60 seconds Buf : 120% Cusp : 40% Tail : 6,000 seconds Chip : 0.1% Stopped : 3 Tip : 300 USDS Chop : 13% Hole : 250,000 Dust : 30,000 A.4.4 - Modification Of stUSDS Risk Parameters (Core) - Except as specified in A.4.4 - Modification Of stUSDS Auction Parameters, the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors, have the ability to modify any of the parameters defined in A.4.4 - stUSDS Risk Parameters. The modification of said parameters is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a Governance Poll. A.4.4 - Modification Of stUSDS Auction Parameters (Core) - A clear justification and analysis must be provided to validate any proposed changes to the Calc , Tau , Buf , Cusp , Tail , Chip , Tip , Chop , or Hole parameters. Before these changes are added to an Executive Vote, the Core Executor Agents must first propose a Governance Poll. However, in an emergency, the Core Executor Agents have the authority to bypass the Governance Poll and add the proposed parameters directly to an Executive Vote. These parameters must be regularly monitored and updated if needed. Add new subdocument of A.4.4.1.2 - SKY-Backed Borrowing (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.4.4.1.2.7 - stUSDS Accessibility Reward (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Accessibility Reward (GitHub) to read as follows: A.4.4 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (Core) - The stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (stUSDS BEAM) enables designated, Governance-whitelisted operators to adjust the stUSDS Rate ( str ), the SKY Borrow Rate ( duty ), the maximum amount that users can deposit into the stUSDS contract ( cap ), and the maximum Debt Ceiling ( line ). Adjustments are governed by the stUSDS BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance. stUSDS BEAM holds four parameters that can be set for each stUSDS parameter: (i) min , (ii) max , (iii) step , and (iv) tau . A.4.4 - Definitions (Core) - The documents herein define the parameters of the stUSDS BEAM. A.4.4 - Min Definition (Core) - The min parameter defines the minimum value for the str and duty parameters that can be set using the stUSDS BEAM. Each of the str and duty parameters has a specific min . A.4.4 - Max Definition (Core) - The max parameter defines the maximum value for the str and duty parameters that can be set using the stUSDS BEAM. Each of the str and duty parameters has a specific max . A.4.4 - Step Definition (Core) - The step parameter limits how much the str and duty parameters can be increased or decreased in a single transaction, bound by the tau parameter. Each of the str and duty parameters has a specific step . A.4.4 - Max Cap Definition (Core) - The maxCap parameter defines the maximum value for the cap parameter that can be set by the stUSDS BEAM. A.4.4 - Max Cap Current Value (Core) - The maxCap is currently set to 1,000,000,000 USDS. A.4.4 - Max Line Definition (Core) - The maxLine parameter defines the maximum value for the line parameter that can be set by the stUSDS BEAM. A.4.4 - Max Line Current Value (Core) - The maxLine is currently set to 1,000,000,000 USDS. A.4.4 - Tau Definition (Core) - The tau parameter defines the minimum time interval, in seconds, that must elapse between consecutive uses or operations of the stUSDS BEAM. A stUSDS BEAM operation may adjust one or more parameters. Once a stUSDS BEAM operation is executed, the tau duration must expire before any subsequent stUSDS BEAM operation can be performed. A.4.4 - Tau Current Value (Core) - The tau is currently set to 57,600 seconds (16 hours). A.4.4 - stUSDS Parameters (Core) - The stUSDS BEAM parameters for each stUSDS parameter set by the stUSDS BEAM are defined in the subdocuments herein. A.4.4 - Str Parameters (Core) - The stUSDS BEAM parameters for the str stUSDS parameter are as follows: max - 5,000 basis points, min - 200 basis points, step - 4,000 basis points. A.4.4 - Duty Parameters (Core) - The stUSDS BEAMparameters for the duty stUSDS parameter are as follows: max - 5,000 basis points, min - 210 basis points, step - 4,000 basis points. A.4.4 - Parameter Adjustments (Core) - All stUSDS BEAM parameters can be modified by the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors. This process will be conducted through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle or, if necessary, through out-of-schedule Executive Votes. A.4.4 - Operators (Core) - The stUSDS BEAM Operators are whitelisted entities that can directly alter the stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM. Changes to stUSDS parameters are limited by the max , min , step , and tau parameters. Operators can be added or removed by an Executive Vote. A.4.4 - Operator Multisig (Core) - The Operator Multisig is an Operator of the stUSDS BEAM and is controlled by Core Executor Agent Atlas Axis. A.4.4 - Operator Multisig Address (Core) - The address of the Operator Multisig on the Ethereum Mainnet is 0xBB865F94B8A92E57f79fCc89Dfd4dcf0D3fDEA16 . A.4.4 - Operator Multisig Required Number Of Signers (Core) - The Operator Multisig currently has a 2/3 signing requirement. A.4.4 - Operator Multisig Signers (Core) - The signers of the Operator Multisig are three (3) addresses controlled by Core Executor Agent Atlas Axis. A.4.4 - Operator Multisig Usage Standards (Core) - The signers of the Operator Multisig must use the multisig to operate the stUSDS BEAM in accordance with the instructions specified in A.4.4 - Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig. A.4.4 - Operator Multisig Modification (Core) - Core Executor Agent Atlas Axis can change the signers of the Operator Multisig at any time, so long as there are at least three (3) signers and at least a majority of signers are required to execute transactions. A.4.4 - Operator Hot Wallet (Core) - The Operator Hot Wallet is a hot wallet controlled by a bot that will update stUSDS parameters on an automated basis as specified in A.4.4 - Automatic Updates By Operator Hot Wallet. The wallet is controlled by Ecosystem Actor TechOps under the supervision of Core Executor Agent Atlas Axis in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors. The addition of the Hot Wallet as an Operator of the stUSDS BEAM is authorized to proceed directly to an Executive Vote without a prior Governance Poll. A.4.4 - Operator Hot Wallet Address (Core) - The address of the Operator Hot Wallet on the Ethereum Mainnet is 0xd06C14820048de2Fb7c9de611EcFdaCE18eC8896 . A.4.4 - Update Of stUSDS Parameters For Hot Wallet (Core) - When the Operator Hot Wallet is added as an Operator of the stUSDS Rate, the stUSDS BEAM parameters must be updated as follows: The step parameters for the str and duty parameters must be reduced to 400 basis points; and The tau parameter must be reduced to 4 hours. These changes are authorized to proceed directly to an Executive Vote without a prior Governance Poll. A.4.4 - Operator Update Process (Core) - stUSDS BEAM Operators can be modified by the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors. This process will be conducted through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle or, if necessary, through out-of-schedule Executive Votes. A.4.4 - Update Process (Core) - The stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM are managed by the stUSDS BEAM Operators as specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Initial Parameter Values Set In Executive Vote (Core) - The initial parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM in the Executive Vote deploying stUSDS and the stUSDS BEAM are: str - 0 basis points duty - 2,000 basis points cap - 200,000,000 USDS line - 200,000,000 USDS A.4.4 - Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig (Core) - Initially, the stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM are managed by the Operator Multisig based on instructions provided by the Stability Scope Advisors. A.4.4 - Request By Stability Scope Advisors (Core) - Any requests to change stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM must be posted to the Sky Forum by the Stability Scope Advisor recommending the change. Once Utilization is below 100% the Stability Scope Advisors should begin recommending changes based on the methodology specified in A.4.4 - Update Methodology but may deviate from the values resulting from this methodology if they determine that other values are advisable to support the growth of stUSDS and the interests of the Sky Protocol. A.4.4 - Operator Execution (Core) - Once a request to change stUSDS parameters has been posted to the Sky Forum by the Stability Scope Advisors, the stUSDS BEAM Operators must prepare and execute the proposed changes in a timely manner. Preparation can include the creation of transaction simulations to verify inputs. A.4.4 - Public Communication (Core) - Once a change in stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM has been executed, the execution must be publicly communicated to the Sky Ecosystem. This communication may take the form of either (1) a Forum post or (2) inclusion of the execution in an informational dashboard that allows community members to see each stUSDS parameter change executed by the stUSDS BEAM. A.4.4 - Automatic Updates By Operator Hot Wallet (Core) - Once the Operator Hot Wallet has been added as an Operator of the stUSDS BEAM (see A.4.4 - Operator Hot Wallet), the stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM must be set by the Operator Hot Wallet. These changes must be based on the update methodology specified in A.4.4 - Update Methodology and the results must be publicly visible on an information dashboard. A.4.4 - Update Methodology (Core) - The documents herein define the methodology that should be used for determining when and how to update stUSDS parameters with the stUSDS BEAM. Initially when stUSDS parameters are set manually by the Operator Multisig (see A.4.4 - Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig) the Stability Scope Advisors may deviate from these parameters in their best judgment. Once the process is fully automated (see A.4.4 - Automatic Updates By Operator Hot Wallet) the automated process must fully conform to the specifications herein. A.4.4 - Conditions For Update (Core) - The stUSDS parameters should be updated if (1) the current Utilization (see A.4.4 - Utilization Definition) deviates from the Utilization as of the last time the stUSDS parameters were set by more than 2.4% and (2) the time since the last update is greater than tau (see A.4.4 - Tau Definition). A.4.4 - Calculations For Update (Core) - The new values for each stUSDS parameter should be set to be as close as possible to the values specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Str Calculation (Core) - The str must be calculated as specified in A.4.4 - stUSDS Rate. A.4.4 - Duty Calculation (Core) - The duty must be calculated as specified in A.4.4 - Rate Setting Formula. A.4.4 - Cap Calculation (Core) - The Stability Scope Advisors must calculate the maximum amount that users can deposit into the stUSDS contract ( cap ) as specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Short Term Calculation (Core) - In the short term while Utilization is above 100%, the cap must be set to 200,000,000 USDS. A.4.4 - Long Term Calculation (Core) - In the long term, the cap must be gradually increased when Utilization is above 85% according to the following formula: cap = 1.2 * current SKY borrowing A.4.4 - Line Calculation (Core) - The Stability Scope Advisors must calculate the maximum amount that users can borrow against their staked SKY ( line ) as specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Short Term Calculation (Core) - In the short term while Utilization is above 100%, the line must be set to 200,000,000 USDS. A.4.4 - Long Term Calculation (Core) - In the long term, the line must be gradually increased when Utilization is above 85% according to the following formula: line = 1.14 * current SKY borrowing Define Resolution Process For Core Simplification Buffer Budget Add a new Article A.5.6 - Core Simplification Buffer Budget (Portal) / A.5.10 - Core Simplification Buffer Budget (GitHub) and subdocuments. This Article should be located directly after A.5.5 - Launch Project (Portal) / A.5.9 - Launch Project (GitHub) to read as follows: A.5.10 - Core Simplification Buffer Budget (Article) - This Article defines the Core Simplification Buffer Budget. A.5.10 - Core Simplification Buffer Budget (Section) - The Core Simplification Buffer Budget is a budget of 10,000,000 USDS and 70,000,000 SKY for certain expenses before those expenses are taken over by the Sky Entities, Agents, or other Ecosystem Actors. A.5.10 - Core Simplification Project Process Resolution (Core) - A one-time transfer of 8,000,000 USDS is hereby authorized to a wallet controlled by the Accessibility Facilitators. This must be the only transfer from the Core Simplification Buffer Budget and once this transfer has been made a subsequent Atlas Edit Proposal must be submitted to delete the Core Simplification Budget entirely. Update Smart Contract Risk Calculations Replace A.3.3.2.1.2.2 - Smart Contract Risk Rating Calculation (Portal) / A.3.3 - Smart Contract Risk Rating Calculation (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Smart Contract Risk Rating Calculation (Core) - The second step in calculating the Instance Smart Contract RRC with respect to an Allocation System opportunity is to calculate the Smart Contract Risk Rating SCRR for the covered smart contracts identified in A.3.3 - Defining Relevant Smart Contracts . The SCRR is calculated as follows: \text{SCRR} = min[\text{CAP}, (\text{SR} + \text{CCR}) \times \text{LAF} \times {AF}] Here min is the mathematical minimum function that returns the lesser of the specified parameters. The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein. Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.2.5 - Audit Adjustment Factor (Portal) / A.3.3 - Audit Adjustment Factor (GitHub) . Add Definitions For Liquidity Layer Parameters In Sky Core Atlas Add a new subdocument of A.2.3.9.1 - Allocation System Primitive (Portal) / A.2.4 - Allocation System Primitive (GitHub) . This document should be located directly before A.2.3.9.1.1 - Allocation System Process Definition (Portal) / A.2.4 - Allocation System Process Definition (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Base Elements (Core) - The documents herein define base elements of the Allocation System Primitive. A.2.4 - Liquidity Layer Parameter Definitions (Core) - The documents herein define common parameters of implementations of the Allocation System based on the Spark Liquidity Layer, including the Grove Liquidity Layer A.2.4 - Rate Limiter (Core) - Rate Limiter refers to the overall mechanism or system that limits the volume of token movements over time, implemented via the RateLimits contracts. The Rate Limiter manages multiple rate limits and enforces constraints on controller operations to prevent rapid asset drainage and mitigate risks from compromised relayers or other attacks. This ensures that the maximum amount of tokens processed within a specific time period stays within safe bounds. The RateLimits contracts and their addresses for each chain can be found in the Allocation System Primitive for a Prime, under ALM Contracts. A.2.4 - Rate Limits (Core) - Rate limits set the maximum allowable amount of tokens that can be processed for specific operations within a given time period. Each rate limit contains the rate limit data: maxAmount , slope , lastAmount and lastUpdated . The current rate limit is calculated using the formula: currentRateLimit = min(slope * (block.timestamp - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount) . The rate limit data maxAmount and slope are configurable parameters that are set and modified by Governance. The rate limit data lastAmount and lastUpdated are internal state data dynamically tracked by the Rate Limiter to perform its calculations. Rate limits set caps on the rate of allocation to a given Instance, they do not act as a limit on the total amount that may be allocated to that Instance. A.2.4 - MaxAmount (Core) - maxAmount sets a hard cap on the level of allocation to an Instance at any given time. It sets the absolute rate limit regardless of how much time has passed since the last allocation. For example, if maxAmount is set to 1,000,000 tokens, the rate limit will increase over time at the rate determined by the slope until it reaches 1,000,000 tokens, at this point the rate limit will stop increasing, but it will resume increasing once an allocation to the Instance has been made. A.2.4 - Slope (Core) - slope is the linear refill rate of a rate limiter’s allowance over time. It defines how quickly the capacity to perform additional inflow or outflow accrues after prior consumption. For example, if the slope is set to 1,000,000 tokens per day (converted to per second for on-chain execution), the rate limit will recover at that rate until it reaches the maxAmount. A.2.4 - LastUpdated (Core) - lastUpdated is the timestamp when the rate limit was last updated, serving as the reference point for calculating time-elapsed refills in the formula. A.2,4 - LastAmount (Core) - lastAmount is the remaining allowance available at the last update, used to compute the current rate limit by adding accrued capacity. A.2.4 - Inflow Rate Limits (Core) - Inflow rate limits constrain the rate at which allocated liquidity can increase into a scope. “Inflow” means movements that raise exposure or capital allocated to an Instance or market, such as depositing, minting, or rebalancing into a position. A.2.4 - Outflow Rate Limits (Core) - Outflow Rate Limits constrain the rate at which allocated liquidity can be withdrawn or exposure reduced from a scope. “Outflow” means movements that lower exposure or capital allocated to an Instance or market, such as withdrawals, redemptions, or unwind operations. Outflow limits are often configured more permissively to prioritize safety and fast exits. When outflow limits are “unlimited,” the rate limits contract simply does not apply a cap in that direction. A.2.4 - Rate Limit IDs (Core) - A Rate Limit ID is a bytes32 key that uniquely identifies a rate limit. Rate Limit IDs allow the system to maintain independent allowance state for each relevant transaction. A.2.4 - MaxSlippage (Core) - maxSlippage is a configurable parameter that sets the maximum allowed price impact or deviation from expected output when executing trades or liquidity operations in a pool. maxslippage is expressed as a decimal and must be a non-zero value. This protects against excessive price impact during volatile market conditions. Make Minor Corrections Replace A.0.1.1.12 - Slippery Slope Misalignment (Portal) / A.0.1 - Atlas Preamble - Definitions - Slippery Slope Misalignment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.0.1 - Atlas Preamble - Definitions - Slippery Slope Misalignment (Core) - Slippery Slope Misalignment is the shortest path to misalignment where incremental misaligned acts are justified in various ways. These can include ignoring the potential significance and larger impact of acts due to their small scale; the trivial way that misalignment occurs; the good intentions of the actor; or the conviction that the ends justify the means. Understanding Slippery Slope Misalignment means understanding that any misalignment at all is always very serious and, if not dealt with, results in increased risk of disequilibrium and alignment failure. In the context of a decentralized ecosystem such as Sky, this could mean a governance attack or financial collapse.
